name: Best Mistakes
definition: For a nonempty binary class $\mathcal H$ on a finite domain $X$, fix a permutation $\pi$ of all of $X$, known to the learner before play. At each coordinate the deterministic learner predicts a label and receives the true label of an unknown fixed target $h\in\mathcal H$. It must predict every coordinate once. Let $b(\mathcal H,\pi)$ be the minimum over learners of the maximum number of mistakes over targets. The **Best Mistakes** parameter is $\min_{\pi}b(\mathcal H,\pi)$. The empty domain has value zero.
graph_summary: Mistake bound under a presentation sequence chosen favorably to the learner.
origin_references: The favorably ordered (best) mistake model is studied in \cite{ben1997online}.

monotonic.proof: A favorable presentation strategy and predictor that works for every target in $\mathcal H$ can be used unchanged when the target is restricted to a subfamily; optimizing over strategies can only improve the bound.

c_monotonic.proof: Restrict an optimal prediction strategy to the conditioned fibre, treating fixed-coordinate labels as known; no additional mistakes are needed.
